rv.q: A rich tapestry of emotions, beautifully conceived and brilliantly performed.

In a longer format, the two halves of the story may become more defined in their own right, at the moment, while their co-existence works well as an exploration of the writer’s craft, they are less effective at charting the course of a relationship.
It’s simply brilliant theatre all round, that rare kind of debut that will blow your mind as easily as it’ll warm your heart.
The performances are very strong, and the creative choices are inspired.
This About Me acutely explores the shifting meanings of intimacy through Grace and Eli, a pair entangled in an intricate, long-standing relationship.
In fact, there’s not much else you’ll be enticed to do other than count the minutes until it’s over.

cn.t: Critics praise this inventive, multimedia exploration of intimacy as a clever meta-theatrical debut, though one dissenter finds it largely hollow. The non-linear structure and mind-bending concept mostly charm, despite questions about its deeper purpose.
